newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn issues warning on Moon's Unification Church.
newsitem.headline: Bonn issues warning on Moon's Unification Church.

text.p: The German government on Tuesday issued a booklet warning against the Unification Church of Korean evangelist Sun Myung Moon.
"The Moon movement obeys the absolute authority of its leader," Family Affairs Minister Claudia Nolte said in a statement.
"For young people and their relatives, joining the movement often means a radical break with their former lives.

"Education, family and friends are often abandoned in favour of complete devotion to the sect. Immaturity and dependency are reinforced by the fact that members make all their possessions over to the group."

The Unification Church says it has around three million followers worldwide and around 1,000 in Germany. Followers believe Sun Myung Moon to be an incarnation of God who is fulfilling the mission of Christ.

Moon was banned from entering Germany last year as a "threat to public safety and order". The German booklet on his movement follows a similarly critical one issued earlier this year on the American-based Church of Scientology.

Scientology has been the target of measures by a number of German regional states who see it as a profit-making group relying on manipulation. Some called for it to be put under surveillance or for members to be banned from public service.
Walter Mueller, spokesman for the Unification movement in Germany, said none of its leaders had been consulted on the latest document.
"That speaks for itself," he said, adding that extracts he had seen were "superficial, sensationalist, over-simplified and say nothing new".
"It is a shame that there hasn't been an attempt as there has in other countries to enter into a constructive dialogue with the principles of the movement," he said.
